[DataSquad's project work grew from {{< var datasquad.tasks_2023 >}} tasks in 2023 to {{< var datasquad.tasks_2025 >}} in 2025.]{.lede}

DataSquad is DSC's peer-consulting model: undergraduate and graduate student
consultants providing sustained project support alongside DSC staff's direct
consultations. Reportable project work grew from **{{< var datasquad.tasks_2023 >}}
tasks in 2023 to {{< var datasquad.tasks_2025 >}} in 2025**, as demand shifted from
one-off consultations toward sustained, hands-on project support. That trajectory
reflects departments increasingly planning research around DataSquad's availability,
not turning to it only when something breaks.

The program started in 2020 on a gift from **Norman Powell**, which funded student
salaries and laptops for the first cohort. The Library added funding in 2023 to
expand the team and add in-person hours. In 2024, DataSquad absorbed the LuxLab
student program after its funding source, CLICC funds, became restricted, merging two
student-support lines into one.

It's also a verified career pipeline, not just a service to faculty: the
{{< var datasquad.placement_cohort >}} cohort has a **{{< var datasquad.placement_rate >}}
placement rate** among its {{< var datasquad.placement_n >}} identified graduates,
including {{< var datasquad.placement_names >}}. Several of the same students worked
on DataSquad's highest-profile faculty projects before landing those placements.
Lawrence Lee, credited above for the Carceral Ecologies speedup, is now a Software
Development Engineer at Amazon.
